items.head: 70fbdd1a5f9008fc4df7dc0050406a17d1b31b4a
items.title: Reduce checksum time when reading ZIP members (R3.12)
items.body:
## Problem
Every CRC-checked ZIP member ran eight polynomial iterations for each output byte. Large stored members spent substantial time verifying their checksum.

## Change
Use a fixed 256-entry IEEE CRC-32 lookup generated at compile time from the existing polynomial. The table occupies 1 KiB; there is no runtime initialization, new dependency, unsafe code or public API change. Initial/final XOR, checksum mismatch errors, output limits and ZIP method support stay unchanged.

Public claim: c787ecc119e4646f14bbe50f0dcd5e13e85c2294. Rebased onto main 22c44d01d271c49187104802459085f273f855f0; final head 70fbdd1a5f9008fc4df7dc0050406a17d1b31b4a. ROADMAP and STATUS are updated.

## Verification
- Four compatibility tests pass on both original and fixed implementations. This is a performance improvement, not a pre-existing correctness failure.
- 732 cases agree with independent Python zlib, including public vectors, 29 fixed length checksums and varied starting offsets. Real stored ZIP reads check every output byte, CRC errors and byte limits.
- Actual release-mode zip::read_entry: five fresh processes per version and member size, 128 MiB of work per process, two warmups, alternating order on the same pinned CPU. All 30 processes produced identical bytes and hashes.
- Median throughput in MiB/s: 64 KiB members 204.708 -> 432.789 (2.114x); 1 MiB 204.351 -> 431.628 (2.112x); 32 MiB 187.751 -> 363.403 (1.936x).
- Rust 1.99.0, identical release settings and dependencies, Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 on AMD EPYC 9V74. The measurements include allocation, copying and CRC checks, but exclude file I/O, decompression, equality checks and deallocation. They do not establish performance on other operating systems or compressed members.
- Original fixed-source full gate: 1,701 passed, 0 failed, 10 existing ignored tests; fmt, strict all-target Clippy, layers, locks, secrets and five-crate Wasm checks passed.
- Exact final-head integration on latest main: 1,707 passed, 0 failed, 10 existing ignored tests; all the same gates passed. ZIP source, new tests, manifests and lockfile have identical Git blob IDs to the measured implementation.

[Compatibility, zlib oracle, benchmark and original full gates](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43038685244)
[Exact final-head integration gates](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43040385017)

No other tool's code, scripts or wording was copied.

items.title: Report incomplete SQLite schemas in database evidence (R3.12)
items.body:
**Roadmap item:** R3.12, SQLite schema completeness.

## Problem
The SQLite b-tree walker already records skipped or unreadable pages and rows, repeated children, and exhausted traversal limits. `whole_schema` discarded that state. A readable prefix could therefore be reported as the complete schema, and a table hidden in an unreadable subtree could receive a definitive absent-table error.

## Change
- Carry the existing incomplete-walk state into `schema()` and `Overview.schema_truncated`, alongside the existing object cap.
- Preserve readable schema objects and table rows. `db_sqlite_show` adds a `schema_incomplete` limitation and partial coverage; a schema-only result has no asserted total. Row paging retains its existing counts and offsets, while the accompanying incomplete schema keeps the overall evidence partial.
- Qualify an unsuccessful table lookup as missing from the readable, incomplete schema. Complete-schema behavior is unchanged.

This covers the schema consumer omitted from #1608, which handled row reads and counts. The walker, SQL parsing, schema field limits and existing row paging remain unchanged.

## Verification
The tests cover complete and empty schema controls, both interior child positions, null/cyclic/reused/missing children, wrong page kinds, invalid cells and root framing, truncation and the depth budget. Engine tests verify retained objects, unknown totals, row-page coverage and qualified missing-table errors.

Python SQLite 3.45.1 generated a 16 KiB database with 163 schema objects on 29 schema leaf pages. Seven damaged/truncated variants and three controls check exact retained object fields and readable rows against SQLite's original queries. Every intentionally damaged schema is also rejected by SQLite's integrity check. A corrupt table-data page with an intact schema remains a schema-completeness control.

Original source 35f113: parser regressions 6 failed/2 passed, engine regressions 4 failed/1 passed, native database comparisons 7 failed/3 passed. Fixed source 6bafba6: all 8 + 5 + 10 passed. Latest-main integration verifies unchanged product, fixture, parser-test, manifest and lockfile bytes; the only regression change replaces `.err().expect()` with the Clippy-required `.expect_err()`.

On main 3a9ad9c6c5de05701d423b8c7e9cc37b550a7170, all touched-crate tests passed: formats 1,711; engine 685; testkit 1 (2,397 passed, 0 failed, 17 existing ignored). Rust 1.99 fmt, strict all-target Clippy for all three crates, layers, locks, secrets and the complete five-crate WebAssembly check passed. Source and lockfile remained clean.

Public claim was pushed before implementation (original 86ebafd; latest-main replay 8554870). The final documentation commit only checks off the ROADMAP claim and adds one STATUS row; it has the same product and tests as the full-gate source fca8b0c.

[Original-source failures, passing controls and fixed native SQLite comparisons](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43046176741)
[Latest-main integration and complete gates](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43047782783)
[Final documentation identity and repository checks](https://github.com/Afloat16/billion-context/actions/runs/43049284010)

The earlier differential run remains red because strict Clippy rejected that test assertion style; its differential and complete test steps passed. The first attempt stopped at a fixture formatting difference before compilation. Both records are retained.

No live application UI or SQLite repair/recovery operation was performed. Tests inspect local fixture files through the actual parser and engine; they do not run user SQL.
